records.text: Paper card. Question: How do high-entropy borides behave under extreme environments of pressures and temperatures?. System: High-entropy transition metal borides, specifically (Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti)B2 and (Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Zr)B2. Processing: High-pressure, high-temperature synthesis using a large-volume Paris-Edinburgh press with a Cupped Drickamer Toroidal cell. Test conditions: Up to 9.5 GPa and 2273 K. Findings: Hexagonal AlB2 phase is stable to high pressures and temperatures; Bulk modulus of 276 GPa at ambient temperature; Compressive yield strength of 28 GPa at 65 GPa; Thermal expansion coefficients calculated; High compressive strength and phase stability make it an ideal candidate for structural material in nuclear and aerospace fields. Mechanism: The high entropy of mixing ensures stability at high temperatures due to lower Gibb’s free energy. Quote: "high-entropy transition metal borides containing a random distribution of five or more constituent metallic elements"
